evidence.excerpt: The ontology models the structure of sandwiches that captures the whole (Sandwich), its parts (BreadSlice, LayerOfFilling, Filling), and six variants (SingleDeckerSandwich, DoubleDeckerSandwich, OpenSandwich, ToastedSandwich, Panini, ClubSandwich).

student_intent.description: Justifying the class and property hierarchy in the ontology

evidence.excerpt:
For classes, Sandwich is placed directly under owl:Thing; everything that is a sandwich inherits from it.
Then, SingleDeckerSandwich, DoubleDeckerSandwich, OpenSandwich,
ToastedSandwich, Panini, ClubSandwich are declared subclasses of Sandwich because
each one is a sandwich with additional constraints.
BreadSlice, LayerOfFilling, and Filling remain siblings of Sandwich because they
are parts of a sandwich, not specialised sandwiches themselves.
For properties, hasBreadSlice and hasLayer are general relations from a sandwich to its
components, so they have no parent other than owl:topObjectProperty.
hasFillingIngredient is a relation from a layer to any ﬁlling. hasMeatFilling and
hasVegetableFilling are declared sub-properties of hasFillingIngredient.

student_intent.description: Discussing the advantages and disadvantages of the ontology structure

evidence.excerpt:
The advantages of this ontology focuses on the structural and compositional aspects of a sandwich, like how many slices of bread it has, how many ﬁlling layers, and the distinction between meat and vegetable ingredients. This will help it to keep a clear and focused scope.
The disadvantage of this structure is that there is little further subdivision of the variants. All variants are below Sandwich, it can be harder to capture more detailed groupings or shared behaviour among subsets of sandwiches.
